name: Salesflare
summary: CRM for small B2B teams that auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar. Deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and basic reporting unless you export.
best_for: small B2B teams whose reps hate data entry: Salesflare auto-logs emails, meetings and contact details from your inbox and calendar
skip_if: you need deep customisation, a big integration marketplace, or built-in calling and invoicing: Pipedrive or a fuller CRM fit better
honest_knock: It's deliberately lean: no built-in dialer, no quoting or invoicing, and reporting feels basic unless you export. Integrations cover the essentials (Gmail, Outlook, Zapier) but niche tools lean on Zapier, and at higher seat counts the price overlaps fuller CRMs. Two further limits come from Salesflare's own help centre. Microsoft 365 users who send campaigns can land on Microsoft's restricted-users list: the article updated 17 September 2026 says this happens when a mailbox exceeds its sending limit or is flagged by spam filters, that Salesflare's own quotas do not always prevent it, and that an admin then has to unblock the user in the Microsoft 365 Defender portal. And the no-limits promise has a fair-use edge, set out in the record-limits article.

pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-14, re-read unchanged 2026-09-27 and again on 2026-10-21 on salesflare.com/pricing, per user a month) Three plans, and the page carries both billing terms plus a $/€ switch: Growth $39 a month or $29 billed annually, Pro $64 or $49, and Enterprise $124 or $99 with a minimum of five users. The euro column prints the same numerals — €39/€29, €64/€49, €124/€99 — so a European buyer pays the same figure in a different currency rather than a converted one. Our earlier reading called this “$29–99 per user” with Growth at about $29–39 and Pro at about $49. The range was right and the label was not: the low number in each pair is the annual rate and the high one is what month-to-month costs, and the five-seat floor on Enterprise never appeared. Lead credits are part of the ladder rather than an add-on — 5 on Growth, 100 on Pro, 250 on Enterprise. There is a 30-day free trial with no card. On that same page the vendor commits to no onboarding fees and to no caps on contacts, users, email templates, tracked emails, custom fields, workflows, dashboards or pipelines.

sessions.what: We tried to sign up for Salesflare by email on 29 October 2026. The route led to a mailbox connection screen, and we stopped there because connecting a real mailbox was outside our test rules. We never got into the CRM, so nothing below is a finding about the product itself.
findings: After the sign-up form, Salesflare showed 'Please fill out your email settings' with fields for email, password and an IMAP server marked as required, plus an optional SMTP server and a Connect button. We saw no skip, later or back option.
Opening the app afterwards showed the login screen, with no signed-in session.

That answers our test question for this route only: the email sign-up we followed asked for a mailbox connection before CRM access. We cannot say whether other routes, such as Google or Microsoft sign-in, work differently; those routes stayed outside the test.
not_tested: Whether the CRM can be used without a mailbox connection by any other route
Everything after sign-up: contacts, import, export and re-import
Checkout, tax and the final price
Support, roles, API access, downgrade and cancellation
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
